author: Faustinus

passages.original: Sabellius enim ipsum di- cit patrem, qui sit et filias, hoc modo, tamquam si unus habeat duo nomina, et interpretator unum ideo dictum, ut unius personae singularitas crederetur. Contra vero Arius respiciens ad hoc qnod ait, sumus, in hoc sermone, pluralitatem intelligens, introduxit impiam pluralitatem deorum, credens unum sempi- ternum Deum, et alium qui esse coeperit Deus; unum omnipotentem, et alium qui non sit omnipotens.
passages.english: For Sabellius says that the Father himself is the one who is also the Son, in this way, as if one [person] had two names, and he interprets "one" as having been said so that the singularity of one person might be believed. Arius, on the other hand, looking to the fact that he says "we are", and understanding plurality in this expression, introduced an impious plurality of gods, believing in one eternal God and another who began to be God; one almighty, and another who is not almighty.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "filias" read as "filius", "interpretator" as "interpretatur", "qnod" as "quod".

passages.original: IV. Non pro impio Photino haec loquimur, qui nu- dum vult esse hominem sine Dei Verbi incarnatione, sed contra Arium antichristum recitamus, qui vult ipsum unigenitum filium, qui est Verbum et sapientia Dei, qua Deum, et non qua hominem crucifixam, et ipsum esse factum Dominum et Christum. Sed etsi durissima obstinatione contendunt dicentes de ipso Deo Verbo scriptum esse, quod Deus illum fecerit et Dominum et Christum;
passages.english: IV. We do not say these things on behalf of the impious Photinus, who wants [Christ] to be a mere man without the incarnation of God the Word, but we set them out against Arius the antichrist, who holds that the only-begotten Son himself, who is the Word and Wisdom of God, was crucified as God and not as man, and that he himself was made Lord and Christ. But even if with the most stubborn obstinacy they contend, saying that it is written of God the Word himself that God made him both Lord and Christ;
passages.notes: "crucifixam" read as "crucifixum". The construction "qui vult ipsum ... crucifixum" lacks an explicit infinitive (presumably "esse" understood); rendered accordingly.
